newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 14.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Ramos on Sunday appointed former Armed Forces chief of staff Arturo Enrile as acting transportation and communications secretary effective April 16. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- President Ramos urged citizens at the weekend to elect a "worthy" president in 1998 so that the political and economic gains achieved during his term will not be wasted. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The peace talks between the government and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) will resume on April 22 and 23 in Cotabato city despite the unresolved shelling issue in Buldon town which nearly caused the collapse of the negotiations. About 11 people were killed in Buldon town last March 16. (STAR)
- The Securities and Exchange Commission plans to revoke the license of brokers circulating rumours to manipulate prices of securities listed at the Philippine Stock Exchange. (JOURNAL)

- Bank lending rates have dropped to an average of 13.1 percent as of March this year compared to the average 15.1 percent a year ago . A central bank source said this reflected the stiff competition in the industry as more banks began operating this year. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The government is set to put a cap on the importation and sale of sensitive agricultural products by duty-free shops in special economic zones such as Subic Bay freeport and Clark special economic zone. (INQUIRER)
